newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's APV approves asset swap with Postabank.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's APV approves asset swap with Postabank.

text.p: Hungary's state privatisation agency APV Rt said on Wednesday it had designated a portfolio worth a nominal 18.2 billion forints ($93.3 million) under a government-approved asset swap with Postabank Rt.
"The market value of the portfolio will be somewhere around 11 billion forints," APV President Arpad Kovacs told a news conference.
The government approved an asset swap worth 17 billion forints between Postabank and APV and said the move was intended to help the bank towards a portfolio that was easier to sell.
Kovacs said Postabank was offering about a dozen real estate items while APV gave minority stakes it owns in several companies.

These include a 21-percent stake in Borsodi Sorgyar, stakes of between 16 and 25 percent in sugar factories Matravideki, Szerencsi and Szolnoki, stakes of under 20 percent in the recently privatised regional gas distributors and stakes of less than five percent in regional electricity suppliers.
International auditor firm Deloitte & Touche will evaluate the Postabank real estate and KPMG will audit the valuation on APV's behalf, Kovacs said.
He said the government-imposed move was in line with APV's business interests.

"Some (Postabank) buildings are near to others already owned by APV thus, a later block sale would be easier," Kovacs said. "The real estates will also facilitate APV to fulfill its obligations to accommodate public institutions."
He said that contrary to earlier press reports, shares in oil and gas company MOL Rt are not part of the package APV offered.
Postabank was hit by rumour-induced withdrawal of deposits worth about 24 billion forints in February.
The Postabank group boosted its balance sheet total to 402.3 billion forints from 281.9 billion in 1996, with most of the increase coming from the bank's expansion.
But profits fell to 184 million forints from 1995's 2.41 billion despite a 12-billion government guarantee on its assets, granted after the withdrawals.

Hungary's bank watchdog APTF said earlier in July that Postabank must stop expanding, concentrate on stabilisation and replace the accumulated loss-making assets with profitable ones even if this causes imminent losses.
